title: Console theme layering and logo-accent overrides for high-contrast dark mode
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: As more customers use custom brand themes and expect a high-quality dark experience, we've observed multiple regressions: chart legends losing contrast, CTA buttons appearing flat when brand accents are applied, and table row dividers collapsing on deep surfaces. This ticket proposes a systematic approach to theme layering and component-level overrides so customer brand palettes remain expressive while meeting accessibility and product hierarchy requirements.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a "surface density" token layer (surface.dense / surface.mid / surface.light) to help map brand palettes into coherent dark surfaces rather than remapping primary tokens directly.
- Define a deterministic accent mapping algorithm (Lch-based contrast-preserving transform) that produces: accent.foreground, accent.border, accent.subtle for each brand color to be used across components.
- Component override rules: buttons, tables, charts, and badges get narrow, prioritized override sets (e.g., button.primary -> allow brand accent for filled state but use neutral token for focus ring unless brand contrast passes AA).
- Chart-specific rules: retain data color saturation, but compute legend/axis/text colors from surface tokens with an adjustable emphasis multiplier to avoid washing out on deep backgrounds.
- Migration & runtime: add compat-layer in component library that accepts legacy brand tokens and synthesizes the full token set at runtime for both hosted and private deployments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Token matrix documented in Confluence with example mappings for 6 real customer brand colors (links below).
- Figma prototypes for table, primary/secondary button, area+line charts showing before/after across three surface densities.
- Unit visual tests (Chromatic/Storybook snapshots) updated for components below, with tolerances defined: buttons, tables, charts, badges, tooltips.
- Engineering API: clear flag to enable "synthesizedBrandTokens=true" with fallback to legacy mapping.
- Accessibility: color contrast checks included in CI that must pass WCAG AA for text and >=3:1 for non-text UI components where feasible.

Design artifacts and references:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/ExAMPLE/console-theming-synthesis (frames: SurfaceDensity / AccentAlgo / ComponentOverrides)
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/573812/Surface+Density+and+Brand+Accent+Mapping
- Prototype recordings: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Example

Rollout plan:
1) Implement token synthesis and feature flag in component library (canary).
2) Ship updated design tokens and Storybook visuals to staging, run visual regression.
3) Gradual rollout: default off for existing customers, opt-in for new themed accounts, force-on for internal teams for verification.
4) Post-rollout: monitor console dashboards for regressions (chart legend clicks, onboarding bug reports).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Perceptual transforms add runtime CPU on initial token synth; mitigate by caching synthesized palettes per tenant.
- Some extreme brand colors will still require a forced neutralization step; we propose an opt-in brand sanitization UI in Console for admins.

Open questions:
- Should emphasis multipliers be exposed in Console theme editor or only available as advanced tokens?
- How to handle legacy CSS custom properties for Private deployments using older component versions?
